settings/cb_hotkey_enabled: Allow opening the menu via hotkey
settings/cb_show_ingame: Show in-game voice packs in settings
settings/cb_show_installed: Show installed voice packs in settings
settings/cb_auto_volume: Apply the preset volume automatically when switching voices
settings/preview_text: This is a typewriter preview sample text used to demonstrate the text speed effect in the general subtitle settings.
settings/cb_sub_update: Allow subtitles to update their content
settings/cb_multi_sub: Allow multiple subtitles at the same time
settings/tooltip/nation_voice:
Nation Voice Settings

Switches the default voice type of the nation voice pack.

Only applies when using a nation voice pack
settings/tooltip/sound_remap:
Sound Remapping

Allows replacing specific in-game sounds, expanding how much a voice pack can modify battle voices.

The remapping scheme is defined by the voice pack and switches together with it.
settings/tooltip/sound_bind:
Sound Binding

Allows playing specified events from a voice pack after certain sounds play or commands are issued — effectively creating a custom "voice event".

The binding scheme is defined by the voice pack and switches together with it.
settings/tooltip/subtitle:
General Subtitle Settings

The settings below only apply to subtitle voice packs; not every voice pack has subtitles. Here you can control how voice pack subtitles are displayed, their speed and their visual effects.
settings/tooltip/subtitle_simple:
Simple Mode

Shows only the speaker's name and the subtitle text. Subtitles no longer use animations in this mode; the typewriter effect is unaffected.
settings/tooltip/subtitle_standard:
Standard Mode

Shows the avatar, title, text and text background.
settings/tooltip/subtitle_update:
Subtitle Content Update

Within a conversation, if consecutive speakers are the same person (same character code), no new subtitle pops up at the transition — the current subtitle is updated instead.
settings/tooltip/subtitle_anim:
Subtitle Animation Effects

Allows subtitles to fade in and then move in a specified way. The plugin currently supports six animations that can be freely arranged: "bubble", "startle", "shake", "wobble", "apology" and "nod".


．Bubble: the subtitle hops up and returns to its original position

．Startle: a faster bubble with a larger movement range

．Shake: the subtitle sways left and right

．Wobble: a faster sway

．Apology: bubble in reverse

．Nod: faster reverse bubble


The movement range depends on the subtitle size, which is determined by the bounding box of its components.
settings/tooltip/multi_sub:
Multiple Subtitles at Once

Allows multiple subtitles to be shown on screen at the same time; a new subtitle does not overwrite the currently playing one.

When disabled, a new subtitle interrupts the current one — only one subtitle is shown at a time.
settings/tooltip/text_speed:
Text Speed

Controls how fast subtitles appear character by character.

Adjustable range: 0~0.1, step 0.01. A speed of 0 disables the typewriter effect.
Recommended: 0.03~0.05.
settings/tooltip/color_scheme:
Color Scheme

Switches the overall color theme of the menu.

Use default — dark theme;
Follow voice pack — automatically uses the current voice pack's theme scheme (if any);
below are the preset themes and the schemes read from voice packs.
settings/tooltip/bg_icon:
Background Icon

Switches the custom images used by menu components, including the left navigation icons and panel background images.

Default — uses the icons on the local disk;
Follow voice pack — automatically uses the current voice pack's icon scheme (if any);
below are the icon schemes read from voice packs.
settings/tooltip/title_text_color:
Title Text Color

Controls the color of the voice pack name at the top of the menu.

Follow color scheme — uses the title color defined by the color scheme;
Custom — manually enter a hex color value (e.g. #FF0000) to change only the title color without affecting other components.
settings/tooltip/title:
Plugin Settings Panel

The settings panel covering most of the features.

Changes are saved immediately and take effect on the next launch.
voice_switch/tooltip/title:
Voice Switching & Sound Playback

．In-game voice packs
Special commander voices included with the client.

．Installed voice packs
Third-party voices loaded from .wotmod files.

．Preview sounds from voice packs
This playlist can be defined by the voice pack and may vary from pack to pack.

Bnk files are loaded dynamically; some bnk files are only loaded during battle, so their events cannot be played in the garage — head to a battle instead.
Note: depending on your client/server, some voice packs may be unusable because they are not actually present in the game's resource files.
voice_switch/tooltip/change_type:
Change Type

Applies to some special crew members — switches their voice type to commander voice or crew voice.

For commanders that have a crew voice, I add a corresponding tag after their name.
voice_switch/tooltip/change_lang:
Change Language

Only applies to some special crew members — switches the voice language. Available languages are broadly RU, EN and CN. Note: The indicated language may not be accurate.

For commanders with voices in multiple languages, I add a corresponding tag after their name.
personal/declaration: Heads-up: the message you send when spotted is a public chat message — everyone can see it and it may be filtered. The client-side rendered replacement text below is only visible to you and only replaces your own messages; it won't be filtered.
personal/alive_desc: When the number of alive teammates is at or below
personal/hint: Clearing the input restores the original game message
personal/spotted_placeholder: Enter the team message to send when spotted...
personal/tooltip/spotted_message:
Speak When Spotted

Automatically sends this message to the team when you get spotted (sixth sense triggers).

Use the placeholder <a> to reference your current minimap position — it can be placed anywhere in the text (or omitted).

Example: I was spotted at <a> → I was spotted at A1
subtitle_settings/tooltip/page_title:
Adjust Subtitle Position

Press "Edit" to enter edit mode, then select the corresponding button to enable dragging of that component. Press the reset button to restore defaults.

In simple mode, only the body text can be adjusted. Subtitle positions are saved separately for simple and standard modes and are saved automatically when you leave the page.
